purpose: Teach: 立ち向かう/人命/自白/撃っ/都知事/親近/疎通/便乗

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、論文、戦時下、本気で、困難に立ち向かう人々、丁寧に、扱っていましたね、本気で、立派、絶対、印象的、本当に。
lines.en: Ren—your paper handled the experiences of people facing wartime hardship with real care and depth.
lines.style: Warm approval, steady eye contact. Opens with his name as genuine recognition. Measured pace, each phrase deliberate. The tone of a teacher who sees real effort.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。人命の重さ、本気で、論文で、扱いました、絶対、本気で、深い、研究、できました、本当に、感謝、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. I tried to treat the weight of human life seriously in the paper—I'm grateful I could do research that deep.
lines.style: Quiet sincerity. No false modesty but genuine humility underneath. Slight hesitation before 'grateful'—he means it. Steady, thoughtful tempo.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦犯の自白記録、本気で、本当に、貴重な、史料、論文で、活用しましたね、本気で、立派、絶対、本当に、感心、本気で。
lines.en: And the way you used those war-crimes confession records as sources—that was really striking work. Genuinely impressive.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost musing. Leans slightly forward with the recognition of difficult material handled with care. Warm but not effusive. The respect in her voice is earned, not given lightly.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。戦時、市民が撃った話、本気で、論文で、扱いました、絶対、本気で、辛い、内容でした、本当に、絶対、感謝、本気で。
lines.en: Yes. I worked with accounts from that time—civilians, the violence—it was hard material to handle, but I'm grateful I could work through it carefully.
lines.style: Careful, measured. A slight lower note on 'hard'—acknowledging the weight without dwelling. Gratitude is genuine and understated. Slow, respectful pacing.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 昔の東京の都知事の影響力、本気で、論文で、扱っていましたね、絶対、本気で、視野、広い、本当に、立派、絶対、本気で、感心。
lines.en: The way you traced the influence of Tokyo's wartime leadership across your whole paper—that was real insight. Your perspective was remarkably broad.
lines.style: Engaged and warm. She's drawn into what he did—this is genuine intellectual recognition. The word 'broad' carries real admiration. Slightly lifted tone, nodding implied.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。戦後、人々が、お互いに、親近感を、本気で、求めた時代、論文で、扱いました、絶対、本気で、深い、研究、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. I tried to show the post-war period—how people were reaching for connection with each other again—I'm grateful that research came together.
lines.style: Reflective, almost turning inward. A quieter delivery this time. There's emotion under the academic language. He's thinking through what he wrote, not just reciting it. Slight vulnerability in the pacing.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦時、敵国との意思疎通、本気で、難しかった歴史、論文で、扱っていましたね、絶対、本気で、印象的、本当に、立派、絶対。
lines.en: The way you worked with the history of wartime communication failures—how hard it was to reach across enemy lines—that was really moving work.
lines.style: Slower, more reflective tone. She's sitting with the weight of what he explored. Genuine contemplation in her voice. Not praise for praise's sake—recognition of something that matters.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。戦後、便乗ビジネス、本気で、増えた歴史、論文で、扱いました、絶対、本気で、社会問題でしたよね、本当に、感謝、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Yes. I looked at the post-war period—how quickly profiteering appeared—it was a real social issue that needed examining. I'm grateful the paper could explore it.
lines.style: Grave and measured. He's made a real connection—this wasn't just academic. The final gratitude lands quietly but firmly. A sense that he knows why this mattered.
